nodes.label: Artel Service (Obsidian Vault Provisioning)
nodes.rationale: Artel automates Obsidian LiveSync vault provisioning via CouchDB, solving the pain of manual CouchDB setup and credential sharing. Design choice: per-user CouchDB accounts (not shared credentials) for isolation.

nodes.label: CouchDB Provisioning (Per-Vault Isolation)
nodes.rationale: Each vault gets a dedicated CouchDB database and per-user CouchDB accounts so credentials are never shared. Atomic creation: PostgreSQL tx + CouchDB HTTP API calls together.

nodes.label: MCP Bearer Token Auth (artel_vtk)
nodes.rationale: Token format artel_vtk_{uuid}_{hex_secret} - UUID identifies the key row, hex_secret is bcrypt-hashed and never stored plain. Shown once to user.

nodes.label: gRPC + grpc-gateway (REST Bridge)
nodes.rationale: Single binary serving both binary gRPC (HTTP/2) and JSON REST on port 1551 via grpc-gateway translation at /api prefix.

nodes.label: verv Scaffold (App Lifecycle Pattern)
nodes.rationale: app.go and config.go are generated and never edited. All wiring goes in custom.go. This enforces a clean separation between generated boilerplate and user business logic.

nodes.label: AES-256 Credential Encryption
nodes.rationale: CouchDB, IMAP, and SMTP credentials are AES-256 encrypted before storage. Key from creds_encryption_key env var. Decrypted in-memory per-request. Prevents credential exposure if DB is compromised.

nodes.label: Feature Sliced Design (Frontend Architecture)
nodes.rationale: Widgets are modular with composable sub-components. Max 3 levels of HTML nesting per component - split into smaller components beyond that. Container/Wrapper CSS naming convention.

nodes.label: Service Layer (Business Logic)
nodes.rationale: Interfaces in internal/service/interfaces.go, implementations in internal/service/v1/. Transport handlers accept service interfaces, never concrete v1 types. Enforces dependency inversion.

nodes.label: Email Credential Lifecycle (Lazy IMAP/SMTP)
nodes.rationale: Clients instantiated per-request (no persistent connections). Credentials decrypted in-memory at call time from email_accounts table.
